value.name: attorney clarifies her limited role
value.description: The attorney tells Mr. Serrano that she represents his mother's estate, not him personally, and suggests he may retain separate counsel.
evidence: "I am going to be very direct with you, Mr. Serrano. I am your mother's estate's attorney. I am not your attorney. If you would like to retain separate counsel I would not advise against it."

value.name: attorney demands Mr. Serrano listen
value.description: The attorney warns Mr. Serrano that she will state her view only once and insists he pay attention.
evidence: "But I am going to tell you what I think, as the person responsible for closing this estate, and I am going to tell you once. Are you listening."

value.name: attorney reveals inheritance terms
value.description: The attorney explains that the mother left the house divided into thirds among Mr. Serrano, his sister, and Rosa.
evidence: "Your mother left you a third of this house. She left your sister a third. She left Rosa a third."

value.name: attorney cites mother's letter
value.description: She tells Mr. Serrano that his mother left him a letter expressing love and stating her view of his role in the family.
evidence: "She wrote you a letter in which she said she loved you and in which she also told you, very clearly, the truth about how she saw the role you had played in this family."

value.name: attorney distinguishes letter from codicil
value.description: The attorney frames the letter as emotionally difficult and the codicil as mere paperwork, saying the hardest part already happened in the dining room earlier that morning.
evidence: "The letter is hard. The codicil is not hard. The codicil is paperwork. The hard part has already happened to you and it happened in the dining room of your mother's house at ten forty-five on a Tuesday morning, and there is nothing I can do about that."
value.location_hint: dining room of your mother's house
value.time_hint: ten forty-five on a Tuesday morning

value.name: attorney offers recovery arrangement
value.description: She offers to record Mr. Serrano's admission that he took the folder without authority and concealed it, so the matter can be treated as an internal estate recovery.
evidence: "What I can do is this. If you tell me now, on the record, that you took the folder from the desk, that you did so without authority, that you concealed its existence from me and from your sister, and that you wish to return it and proceed in accordance with your mother's wishes — if you tell me that, then I will document it as a recovery, and the question of what you did with the folder during those six days becomes a matter of the estate's internal accounting, and not a matter for anyone else."

value.name: attorney warns of consequences for refusal
value.description: The attorney warns that if Mr. Serrano does not make the admission, or if he does and then fails to comply, the issue will escalate beyond the estate.
evidence: "If you do not tell me that, or if you do tell me that and"
